content: Man, when perfected, is the best of animals, but when separated from law and justice, he is the worst of all.
author: Aristotle
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Water is the softest thing on earth, yet it carves through solid granite. It doesn't fight obstacles; it yields, flows around them, and quietly finds its way to its natural level.

In Aristotle's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. When we force outcomes with brute willpower and anxiety, we exhaust ourselves and create unnecessary resistance. Aligning with nature means trusting the timing of things and moving with steady, patient persistence.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
